克農鑼主要出現在印尼爪哇甘美蘭合奏中，作為鑼點結構的一部分，標示大鑼之間較小的段: The kenong appears mainly in the Javanese gamelan ensemble of Indonesia, as part of the gong punctuation, marking off the smaller sections between the large gongs. In a fast, short structure the interval between strokes can be as little as about a second; in a longer gendhing or at a slow irama level it can last several minutes. When playing, the kenong is often the responsibility of the same player as the kempyang and ketuk, and it stands with gong-type instruments such as the bonang and kempul in the gamelan line-up.
克農鑼主體採用青銅或黃銅等金屬材料鑄造而成，具有優良的共鳴性能。鑼身表面經過精心: The body of the kenong is cast from bronze, brass or another metal and resonates well. The surface of the gong is polished with care to get the best sound. The head of the beater is usually of wood, taller and heavier than a bonang beater so as to produce a strong, forceful tone. The wooden beater is sometimes wrapped in leather or cotton cloth to soften the timbre while keeping it bright and loud.
克農鑼屬體鳴樂器，側放於箱架。其槌較bonang所用者高，聲音因音色突出而易辨。: The kenong is an idiophone, set on its side on a box stand. Its beater is taller than the one used for the bonang, and its sound is easy to pick out because the timbre stands forward. Beside the bonang, kempyang and ketuk, which are also rack gongs, the kenong is usually larger but markedly higher in pitch. A set of kenong is tuned to different pitches according to the slendro and pelog tuning systems, and marks off sections smaller than the gongan in the gamelan's punctuation.
克農鑼是印尼爪哇甘美蘭合奏使用的體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號: The kenong is an idiophone used in the Javanese gamelan of Indonesia, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.241.21. It belongs to the gong family and is set on its side, much as wide as it is long, and with the bonang, kempyang and ketuk it is a rack gong; it is usually larger and higher in pitch. The player strikes it with a taller beater and sometimes also plays the kempyang and ketuk, marking the smaller rhythmic structures in gamelan music.
克農鑼橫置於框架（rancak），通常一至兩面排成線或弧，圍繞演奏者。演奏以克農: The kenong rests horizontally on a frame (rancak), usually one or two of them in a line or an arc around the player. It is struck with a kenong beater, which is taller than the bonang beater. A beginner first works out where it sits in the gamelan's punctuation: it marks the smaller sections inside the interval between the large gongs (the gongan), and the interval between its strokes is called the nongan; in a fast short structure that is about a second, in a long piece at a slow irama level it can be several minutes. There is usually one kenong for each note, with substitutes when a note is missing; sometimes the kempyang and ketuk are played by the same person.
克農鑼為甘美蘭音樂中的鑼類樂器。多數甘美蘭樂器源自印尼爪哇，並傳布至東南亞。來源: The kenong is a gong-type instrument of gamelan music. Most gamelan instruments come from Java in Indonesia and spread through Southeast Asia. The source gives no specific years, names or further detail on its development, so its history can only be confirmed as bound up with the Javanese gamelan tradition and as current in Southeast Asian music.
